clue.text: Occasional butt from goat following girl

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the animal's word is placed behind the girl's name

parts.note: a girl's name, also a month
a silly goat is a fool

explanation.surface: A goat that follows a girl about gives her an occasional headbutt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the goat's word after the girl's. 'Following' here orders the pieces; the butt is a joke's victim, not a goat's charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The victim of a first-of-April hoax is the target of a joke only on that one day each year, hence an occasional butt.

clue.text: Plea to the pleader

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a request addressed to God
second meaning: one who prays, pronounced with the stress on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: The same spelling covers both the request and the person making it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest request to God, and a person who prays can also be called a prayer.

clue.text: Confine one after another, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the sound of the phrase matters, not its spelling

parts.note: doing things one after another is doing them in turn

explanation.surface: Someone is told to lock people up one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to detain or imprison someone, especially an enemy alien in wartime, which is to confine them.

clue.text: Softer sort of wood

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant version, so the letters come out rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A carpenter describes a timber as a softer kind of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Softer sort of wood' reads like softwood timber; the wood is a stretch of trees instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is a large area covered with trees, which is what a forest is.

clue.text: Carole's making announcements

indicators.note: making suggests building something new from the material named, so its letters are reworked

parts.note: the name with its possessive s, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A woman called Carole is busy making public announcements.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracles are pronouncements delivered by a prophet or god, so solemn announcements.

clue.text: He takes pains to provide pleasure

definitions.text: He takes pains to provide pleasure

parts.words: He takes pains to provide pleasure
parts.note: surface reading: someone who works diligently to please others
setter's reading: he literally accepts pain, and that is what gives him pleasure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes pains' normally means makes an effort; here it means receives pain, and the pleasure is his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person derives enjoyment from suffering pain, so accepting hurt is the source of delight.

clue.text: Cook's vessel, one seen in rain, beam obscured

indicators.note: something seen in a thing is placed inside it
obscured suggests confused and made unclear, so the combined letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cook's pot stands outside in the rain, with a sunbeam hidden by cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: One goes inside rain, then the lot is mixed with beam to give BAIN-MARIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bain-marie is a pan of hot water in which a cook stands a dish for gentle heating, a kitchen vessel.

clue.text: Fast plane is not re-ordered, so initially gets rid of the cargo

indicators.note: things re-ordered are put into a different sequence

parts.note: a jet is a fast aircraft
the two words rearranged

indicators.note: initially points to the very start of the word next to it

parts.note: first letter of so

explanation.surface: A speedy aircraft that hasn't been rescheduled dumps its freight.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw goods overboard from a ship or aircraft, getting rid of the load.

clue.text: Easter display — of troops?

parts.note: first reading: the festive procession in Easter bonnets
setter's reading: the same word for soldiers marching in review

explanation.walkthrough: An Easter parade is a procession in fine spring clothes; troops also go on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a public procession or display, whether by holiday crowds in finery or by soldiers drilling.

clue.text: Fast finish

parts.note: surface reading: a speedy ending to a race
setter's reading: a period of fasting, namely Lent, whose last day leads into this festival

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective for a sprint finish; it is the noun, the Lenten fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent's forty days of fasting end with the celebration of the Resurrection, so that Sunday marks its completion.

clue.text: Capital investment for Easter

parts.note: surface reading: putting money into a business
setter's reading: capital means the head, and to invest once meant to clothe, so headwear

explanation.walkthrough: Capital comes from the Latin for head, and invest has an old sense of dressing someone; an Easter bonnet is decorated headwear for the festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat tied under the chin, traditionally trimmed with flowers for the spring festival, is something one puts on the head.

clue.text: Retaliation concerning April's odd tricks ultimately

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the month with its s, letters rearranged

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: last letter of tricks

explanation.surface: Someone gets their own back for the strange pranks played on the first of April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' tempts you to take alternate letters of April's; it is an anagram signal instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprisals are acts of revenge taken in return for an injury, which is retaliation.

clue.text: Cuts and shares out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are put in fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slices something up and hands out the portions.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to clip or trim with a blade, as with fleece, so the verb means cuts.

clue.text: Did not turn out as intended

definitions.text: Did not turn out as intended

parts.words: Did not turn out as intended
parts.note: surface reading: a plan that went wrong
setter's reading: turn out means get out of bed, and he failed to rise at the planned time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' suggests an outcome; read it as rising in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stayed asleep past the alarm failed to get up at the time they meant to.

clue.text: Realistic sort of joke for today

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sensible and down to earth
second meaning: a physical trick played on someone, fitting for the first of April

explanation.walkthrough: Today is the first of April, the date of this puzzle, when tricks are traditional.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical means concerned with real outcomes rather than theory, and a practical joke is a prank played on somebody.

clue.text: Belt buckles worn by men

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the items themselves

parts.note: to belt someone is to hit them, as is to cuff
buckles and links are both fastenings

explanation.surface: A list of men's accessories: belts and their fasteners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' looks like the garment; it is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirt-sleeve fasteners are jewellery traditionally worn by men with formal shirts.

clue.text: A fool to be taken for a ride, not only today

definitions.text: to be taken for a ride
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a donkey, an animal people ride on

explanation.surface: Someone duped on the first of April, though such dupes exist all year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken for a ride' suggests being conned; here it is literal, an animal ridden on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a silly person and a donkey, the beast children ride at the seaside.

clue.text: A couple of pounds for the lot

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound, twice over

explanation.surface: A shopper is offered everything on the stall for two quid.
explanation.definitionFit: The lot means everything, the whole amount, which is what this word signifies.

clue.text: Look for a mole

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to catch sight of something
second meaning: a secret agent planted inside an organisation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Look for a mole' reads as hunting the burrowing animal or a traitor; 'for' simply links two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to see or watch; as a noun it is a secret agent, which a mole is in espionage.

clue.text: Equivalent to 15
A "Look Back in Anger" sort of play?

definitions.text: A "Look Back in Anger" sort of play?

parts.words: "Look Back in Anger" sort of play
parts.note: surface reading: a drama in the style of John Osborne's 1956 kitchen-sink play
setter's reading: a strong feeling such as rage gives its name to the Easter drama of Christ's suffering

explanation.walkthrough: Look Back in Anger is a famous British stage play; the answer is both intense emotion and the Easter play retelling the Crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion means intense emotion such as rage, and a Passion play dramatises Christ's suffering at Easter.

clue.text: Non-professional way to provide a 31?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not of the clergy or a profession, amateur
second meaning: what a hen does to produce an egg; 31 is EASTER EGG

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 31 across, EASTER EGG, and a hen produces eggs by laying.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay describes people outside a profession or the clergy, and a bird lays eggs.

clue.text: State of a student gaining a degree, then another

parts.note: taken as written
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
the second a, taken as written after the link gaining
Bachelor of Arts
another degree, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A student's progress: a first degree, then a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Fierce storm on the coast of Brazil

definitions.note: a phrase describing a place, standing for the city itself

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A violent storm batters the Brazilian shoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fierce storm' reads as adjective and noun; storm is the verb signalling a mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Recife is a large port city in north-east Brazil, lying on the Atlantic seaboard.

clue.text: Pretend to have influence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put on a manner or feign a feeling
second meaning: to produce a change in something

explanation.surface: Someone fakes having clout.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect can mean to feign, as in affecting indifference, and also to act upon or change something.

clue.text: He's in charge, but has a leader

definitions.text: He's in charge, but has a leader

parts.words: He's in charge, but has a leader
parts.note: surface reading: a boss who still answers to someone higher
setter's reading: a leader is a newspaper's main opinion column, which this boss controls

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a newspaper's leader is its editorial article, so the person in charge of the paper has one.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a newspaper runs the publication and is responsible for its opinion columns.

clue.text: Taking flight, running fast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: travelling through the air
second meaning: moving at great speed

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing, sprinting away at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes travel through the air on wings and also any very rapid movement, such as a sprinter's dash.

clue.text: Five hundred wrongly laid off on Sunday — they are out now

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the words have been set down incorrectly and need rearranging

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
the two words rearranged
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: Five hundred workers were wrongly sacked on a Sunday and are now out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' suggests being out of work; it means in bloom, as spring flowers are in April.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow spring flowers bloom around April, so at the time of the puzzle they are out, meaning flowering.

clue.text: Stored face backwards in the end

indicators.note: backwards means the word is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: a clock's face is its dial
taken as written, placed at the end

explanation.surface: Someone put a clock face away backwards in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' does double duty: in is the word itself and the end is where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay in supplies is to store them up for future use, so laid in means stocked or stored.

clue.text: Marsh plant providing a variety of materials

indicators.note: a variety implies different forms, so the letters take another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wetland plant supplies a range of raw materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's-tail is an aquatic plant with whorled leaves growing in ponds and marshy ground.

clue.text: Second thoughts about offensive jokes played today

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part wraps around the other

parts.note: a postscript is the afterthought added at a letter's end
rank means foul or offensive, as of a smell

explanation.surface: Someone has misgivings about tasteless tricks played on the first of April.
explanation.walkthrough: Second thoughts tacked onto a letter are a postscript, abbreviated in two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: April Fool's Day is the day for practical tricks, so pranks are the jokes played on this date.

clue.text: Segregate something that may be present

indicators.note: something a word may be is what it could turn into once its letters are moved

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to set aside an item that might be a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate egg is a traditional gift given at the spring festival, so it is a present.
